hypotheses: If wider policy inputs and changed initialization explain the gap, retaining the IPPO local trunk and adding zero-initialized residual intention projections should improve fixed-budget development endpoints.
If useful intention conditioning is learned, enabled residual fusion should improve over the same residual model trained with all peer gates disabled.
If input-induced feature drift still dominates, the enabled residual model may trail its paired disabled-input ablation despite identical initial local policy.
limits: Experimental redesign, not a proven bug fix or performance improvement.
Same initialization does not imply matching IPPO training RNG after auxiliary sampling.
One training seed, two tasks, development only; no held-out seeds or best-checkpoint selection.
Disabled-input models are mechanism ablations and cannot be promoted as DMS.
